newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Jardines mulls T$12 bln Taiwan ventures.
newsitem.headline: Jardines mulls T$12 bln Taiwan ventures.

text.p: International trading group Jardine Matheson Holding Ltd said it was mulling investing some T$12 billion in Taiwan over the next three to five years.
"We have the idea to invest some T$12 billion in Taiwan over the next three to five years," a company executive in Taipei told Reuters by telephone.
"The exact amount of investment will depend on the opportunity of the Taiwan market," the executive, who declined to be identified, said.
"Taiwan is one of our major investment targets," the executive said.
At present, Jardine Matheson Holdings invests an average T$1-2 billion in Taiwan per year, he said.
The group's Taiwan operations include fast-food chain stores, supermarkets, furniture and securities brokerages.
Jardine Matheson's planned expansions in Taiwan had no direct relations with Hong Kong's July 1 handover to China, the executive said.
The Hong Kong-based Jardine Matheson has repeatedly pledged its commitment to Hong Kong and communist China, although its relations with Beijing have at times been marked by controversy.
Jardine Group is a major colonial trading house whose history in Hong Kong dates back to its early opium trading days.

It was not immediately clear how China's leaders would interpret a major Jardine expansion in Taiwan, seen by Beijing as a rebel-held province since a 1949 civil war split left it in the hands of the defeated Chinese Nationalists.

Jardines angered Beijing when it shifted its domicile to Bermuda from Hong Kong in 1984 -- the year when Beijing and London signed the Sino-British Joint Declaration laying plans for Hong Kong's 1997 return to Chinese rule.
China once branded Jardines "the black sheep of business".
The group's companies were delisted from the Hong Kong stock exchange in 1994 and 1995.
Group chairman Henry Keswick has tried to improve ties, meeting with Chinese Vice-Premier Zhu Rongji and other leaders to stress Jardines' desire to expand in China.
The Jardine executive in Taipei said the company had global ambitions that went far beyond Hong Kong.
"We are an international company, not just a Hong Kong company," the executive said.
